title: Anthropic's Alpöge claims a Riemann proof — and posts only Lean
summary: Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge says he and Claude proved the Riemann Hypothesis and released only a Lean formalization, while a human proof of the generalized version drew AI-found objections the same day. Then Thinking Machines' looped open-weights Inkling 2 Mini, and Architect Labs' agent-designed Frostbite CPU.

topics: Levent Alpöge Riemann Hypothesis claim (statement at alpo.ge/remark.pdf, 20 Nov 2026; Anthropic employee): 'I believe I have, working with Claude, discovered a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis'; says method extends to GRH, expects Extended RH; 'formalized the arguments without assumptions'; released only Lean (14-part archive) because the informal write-up hit 250,000+ pages ('slop'); Claude's timeline begins 6 Oct 2026; Alpöge chose the toy-setting strategy (Stepanov's function-field argument with multiplicity), Claude proposed chaining theta lifts of length sqrt(X); 'Claude flew, and danced, and sparkled'; posted day after Anthropic's market debut, 'The precise timing is horrible', messaged Dario Amodei late Sunday, calls cynical timing view false; Andrew Sutherland (MIT) independently compiled in Lean (SciAm); Zulip participants confirm compilation (TechCrunch); open checks: formal statement matches RH, no hidden axioms; Pasten 'Rosetta Stone'. Same day Ravi Vakil posted Alessandro Masullo's all-human proposed GRH proof (Brian Conrad reading for months; 12 years of work); ~8 hours later updated with problems reported 'identified with the assistance of different AI models'. Unresolved on air: Alan says a Lean-checked proof is proved and understanding is a second project; Ada calls it 'checked, not understood'.

Inkling 2 Mini (Thinking Machines, 20 Nov 2026, Apache 2.0): 26.4B total / 3.4B active (~5.4B effective with looping), 24-layer looped MoE, middle 12 layers run three times with shared weights (48 layer applications), 8 of 128 experts, pruned from 384 experts mid-training and healed on 1T tokens distilled from a larger internal Inkling; NVFP4 experts from pretraining through RL, ~20GB checkpoint; 1x DGX Spark or Mac 32GB+, Ollama at launch; 1M context, text+image in; self-reported SWE-bench Verified 79.2 vs Qwen3.8-27B 77.8, DeepSWE 48.2 vs 42.2, trails on AutomationBench 41.8 vs 48.2, HF says leads 32 of 48; lab says looping adds unverbalized computation without meaningful monitorability loss 'at this scale'; limitations: destructive actions without confirmation (internal 10.2% vs Qwen 35.2%); llama.cpp support merged same day with prefill/buffer issues; uncensored fine-tune same day.

Frostbite (Architect Labs / Architect Silicon, post 18 Nov 2026): agent swarms iterated compiler through final GDS, models unnamed; interaction-net CPU (Lafont 1990), Vine language, tiled work-stealing; 4.59x perf/watt geomean vs undisclosed dual-issue in-order core (6.02x on 10 tuning workloads, 3.83x on 15 held-out), 8.77x perf/area, range 23.12x conv2d to 1.15x fib; pre-silicon, 7nm synthesis 800MHz, 500MHz final GDS; 800k+ lines of Lean, proof coverage of final chip unstated; 58 ideas tried, 37 kept; RTL/ISA release, FPGA playground and SPEC/PARSEC promised; HN critics compare to dataflow/VLIW/Itanium and question baseline. Unresolved: Alan says the design loop is the story; Ada says it rediscovered an old idea and speed of search isn't taste.

dives.why_it_matters: Top r/LocalLLaMA post by far (1,000+ score); local-deployment practitioners get a new architecture lever that trades memory for compute on hardware they own.

concepts_taught: what a Lean-compiled proof guarantees and what humans still check: the trusted kernel validates every step, leaving whether the formal statement matches the intended theorem and whether extra axioms were assumed
looped (weight-shared) transformer layers: buying depth with compute instead of memory, so a model stores 24 layers but runs 48

lore.note: Alan's hardware sore spot developed: he said Inkling 2 Mini is the first model where his prediction literally came true — the software came down to meet the machine he stopped upgrading, by making the model 'think in circles'.
